$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.core. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-REWRITE-MEMO-OFF
arms.note: the pass rewrites a shared Doc node once per path to it, so a nest of two-branch ctors is rewritten 2^depth times

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-SUBTREE-MEMO-OFF
arms.note: every subtree question walks a shared node once per path to it, 2^depth on a nest of two-branch ctors

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-COMMIT-MEMO-OFF
arms.note: committing an opened paren re-commits a shared node once per path to it

arms.name: M-TERNARY-TAIL-GATE-OFF
arms.note: a ternary after a paren group that opens glues its `? a : b` onto the closing `)` line with no width check, so the line overflows or the else branch breaks its own arguments

arms.name: M-TERNARY-TAIL-GATE-NESTED-OFF
arms.find: return ternaryTailGate(d, opened, decisions, width) ?? WrapBoundary(opened);
arms.note: a ternary nested inside a committed glue keeps its `? a : b` on its condition's closing line whatever its width

arms.name: M-TERNARY-TAIL-GATE-OFF-BY-ONE
arms.note: a closing line one column past the limit still carries the ternary tail

arms.name: M-TERNARY-TAIL-REST-OFF
arms.note: what follows the ternary on its tail line (`),` / `);`) is not charged, so a glued tail overflows by that much

arms.name: M-TERNARY-TAIL-FLAT-WIDTH
arms.note: a branch that opens its own paren group is counted flat, so `) ? x && (` breaks its seams although that line fits

arms.name: M-TERNARY-TAIL-BREAKS-CHARGES-REST
arms.note: a tail whose branch breaks is charged the `);` that lands on a later line, so a fitting first tail line breaks its seams

arms.name: M-TERNARY-TAIL-BREAKS-OFF-BY-ONE
arms.note: a first tail line ending where a branch opens its group glues one column past the limit

arms.name: M-TERNARY-HEAD-GATE-OFF
arms.note: the head line of a glued ternary is not width-checked, so a condition head past the limit keeps the tail glued behind it

arms.name: M-TERNARY-HEAD-LIMIT-LOW
arms.note: a head line of exactly the limit counts as overflowing, so the ternary breaks its seams although the head fits

arms.name: M-TERNARY-REST-AWARE-GLUE-OFF
arms.note: a rest-aware ternary whose condition closes an opened group is never glued, so its `?` / `:` always break although the tail fits

arms.name: M-TERNARY-CLOSING-GATE-OFF
arms.note: the `) : else` line of an opened then-branch is not width-checked, so it overflows the limit

arms.name: M-TERNARY-CLOSING-REST-OFF
arms.note: what follows the else branch on the `) : else` line is not charged, so that line overflows by that much

arms.name: M-TERNARY-CLOSING-ELSE-BREAKS-CHARGES-REST
arms.note: an else branch that breaks on the `) : else` line is charged the content that lands on a later line, so a fitting closing line breaks the seams

arms.name: M-TERNARY-CLOSING-ELSE-BREAKS-OFF-BY-ONE
arms.note: the `) : else` line of an else branch that breaks on it glues one column past the limit

arms.name: M-TERNARY-ELSE-BREAKS-UNDETECTED
arms.note: an else branch that breaks on the `) : else` line is not recognised, so the rest after it is charged to that line although it lands later

arms.name: M-OPEN-HEAD-NEVER-CROSSES
arms.note: a lambda body that opens its own construct always stays glued to the arrow, so a head that runs past the line is no longer moved below it

arms.name: M-OPEN-HEAD-ALWAYS-CROSSES
arms.note: a lambda body that opens its own construct always moves below the arrow, so a head that fits beside it no longer glues

arms.name: M-TERNARY-HEAD-PENDING-OFF
arms.find: final effPending: Int = n > width ? pendingSpace : 0;
arms.note: a strict-limit first-line probe ignores the separator still pending before it, so a head after `= ` glues one column past the limit

arms.name: M-PROBE-SEARCH-REVISITS
arms.note: the collapse-probe search re-walks a shared Doc node once per path to it, 2^depth on a nest of two-branch ctors

arms.name: M-PAREN-SIBLING-FLAT
arms.note: a paren-open probe measures the rest of its line flat, so the leftmost of two paren operands opens although only the second crosses the limit

arms.name: M-PAREN-SIBLING-COLLAPSE
arms.note: a collapse-candidate paren counts as a break point although it may stay glued at the expression tail, so the paren before it glues and the line overflows

arms.name: M-PAREN-LIST-BREAK
arms.note: an argument list that crosses the limit is not seen breaking by itself, so the fitting paren before it opens instead

arms.name: M-PAREN-FLATTEN-REGION
arms.note: a paren inside a pinned-flat argument list counts as a break point, so the paren before it glues and the line overflows

arms.name: M-PAREN-SIBLING-FORCE-FLAT-FRAME
arms.find: final frameSibling: Null<RestSibling> = f.forceFlat ? null : sibling;
arms.note: a probe in a force-flat frame counts as a break point, so the paren before it glues and the line overflows

arms.name: M-PAREN-EXACT-CONTENT
arms.note: a paren whose own content can break trusts the columns after it, glues, and its lambda breaks against a rest it no longer counts

arms.name: M-PAREN-EXACT-REST
arms.note: a rest node measured on a guessed flat side keeps the column exact, so a group after it is predicted to break at a column render never reaches

arms.name: M-PAREN-CHAIN-PREDICTS
arms.note: a method-chain probe trusts a later argument list's break, keeps its link glued, and the short call breaks instead

arms.name: M-PAREN-EXACT-SOFT-BOUNDARY
arms.note: a soft break under a WrapBoundary inside a Flatten reads as flat, though render restores break mode there, so the asker trusts columns it never reaches

arms.name: M-PAREN-SIBLING-OFF-PATH
arms.note: a paren on the flat side of an unresolved probe counts as a break point, though render may take that probe's break side and run the line on

arms.name: M-PAREN-PENDING-LAST-ONLY
arms.note: only the last of several held-back spaces stays out of the column, so a plain group that fits is predicted to break

arms.name: M-PAREN-ALT-ROUTE
arms.note: a walk a later paren ends answers the walked route only, though render may take an unresolved probe's break side and run the line on past that paren

arms.name: M-PAREN-ALT-SURPLUS
arms.note: an untaken side that runs on past its node without breaking adds nothing, so a group that breaks onto its wider IfBreak side is measured too short

arms.name: M-PAREN-RUNON-SUSPEND
arms.note: a prediction inside the walked side of a node whose untaken route runs on ends the walk, so what follows the node on that route's line is never counted

arms.name: M-PAREN-RUNON-RESUME
arms.note: a run-on route's suspension outlives its node, so a later paren after the node no longer ends the line and the fitting asker opens

arms.name: M-PAREN-RUNON-FRAME
arms.note: a run-on route's suspension survives its frame, so a later paren in the next frame no longer ends the line and the fitting asker opens

arms.name: M-RESTPROBE-COLUMN-GUESS
arms.note: a rest-aware group predicts nothing about the rest of its line, so an anon type hint is weighed against the full flat width of an initializer that breaks anyway and breaks itself

arms.name: M-RESTPROBE-COLUMN-FLAT
arms.note: a rest-aware group predicts the rest from its flat-layout column, so a trailing list that breaks only because the group stayed flat is taken as a break of its own and the group stays flat over it

arms.name: M-RESTPROBE-FULL-LINE
arms.note: a later full-line probe ends a rest-aware group's line too, so a call stays flat and its chain link breaks, opening only because the call did not

arms.name: M-REST-FORCEFLAT-FRAME-INEXACT
arms.note: a force-flat frame ends the column predictions even when it renders as measured, so an anon nested in a flat hint is weighed against the literal behind the hint and breaks inside it

arms.name: M-REST-GROUP-FRAME-INEXACT
arms.note: a force-flat tail holding a second nested anon ends the column predictions for a group asker, so the first nested anon breaks inside a flat hint

arms.name: M-REST-GROUP-NODE-INEXACT
arms.note: a rest-aware group in a group asker's rest ends the column predictions, so a later literal that breaks by itself is measured flat

arms.name: M-PENDING-HARDLINE-BLANK-FLUSHED
arms.note: a blank gap flushes a pending forward hardline and is written after it, so the keyword after `} // c` lands one space past the indent

arms.name: M-BREAK-EVERY-NODE
arms.note: every node of a break is offered again by every list it is nested in, so the alternatives, and the Doc, grow exponentially with the nesting depth

arms.name: M-PAREN-MEASURES-COMMITTED
arms.note: an expression paren measures a committed literal break deferred, so the paren that opens for every narrower literal glues once the literal breaks: one write still, but onto the other fixed point than the one the paren reached before

arms.name: M-BREAKMARK-SITE-OFF
arms.note: an `#if` branch literal that breaks by its own width decision is no longer named, so a list around it lays itself out from the flat item and the next write, reading the broken literal back, lays the list out by the multi-line-item rules

arms.name: M-BREAKMARK-UNRECORDED
arms.replace:
stack.push(new Frame(f.indent, f.mode, inner, f.forceFlat, f.hardFlat));
			case BreakCommit(_, flat):
arms.note: the measure render no longer records a rendered `BreakMark`, so no named literal ever resolves its `BreakCommit` to the read-back layout

arms.name: M-BREAKMARK-UNREAD
arms.note: the measure's recorded `BreakMark`s are not read as taken breaks, so the read-back layout is never picked

arms.name: M-BREAKMARK-ONE-ROUND
arms.note: the committed layout is not measured again, so a literal that only the committed layout pushes past the limit (a call that opens around a comprehension) breaks un-read-back

arms.name: M-BREAKMARK-REBUILD-FRESH-TOKEN
arms.note: a rebuilt `BreakMark` loses its token, so a copy a list lays out names a break no `BreakCommit` waits for

arms.name: M-REGION-SEAMS-SOFT
arms.find: case Line(flat, verbatim) if (flat != '\n'): Line('\n', verbatim);
arms.replace: case Line(flat, verbatim) if (false): Line('\n', verbatim);
arms.note: the read-back form keeps soft seams, so the list measures the broken region as flat as before

arms.name: M-REGION-MARK-ALWAYS
arms.note: the mark renders whether or not the group breaks, so a region that fits is committed broken

arms.name: M-NESTED-THROUGH-BODIES
arms.note: the walk descends fit bodies whatever the caller asked

arms.name: M-WIDTH-RULE-DECISION-UNREAD
arms.note: a literal broken by a lineLength rule is no width decision to the shared reader, so its comprehension body stays glued and the next write moves it Allman

arms.name: M-TCO-OVERWIDE-CODE-MOVED
arms.find: end >= 0 && end <= n && end + trailWidth > n
arms.note: the comment moves off code that is over the width on its own, where moving it fixes nothing the knob promises

arms.name: M-TCO-BOUNDARY
arms.find: end >= 0 && end <= n && end + trailWidth > n
arms.replace: end >= 0 && end <= n && end + trailWidth >= n
arms.note: a line landing exactly on the width reads as overflowing, so a comment that fits moves

arms.name: M-TCO-MULTILINE-MOVED
arms.find: final end: Int = naturalSingleLineEnd(code, col, f.indent, width);
arms.replace: final end: Int = naturalFirstLineWidth(code, col, f.indent, width);
arms.note: the probe measures the code's FIRST line, so code that spans lines on its own loses the comment from its last line whenever the first line plus the comment is wide

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-CHAIN-GROUP-PLAIN-ONLY
arms.find: case GroupWithRestProbe(inner): { inner: inner, restAware: true };
arms.note: CollapsePass no longer recognises a rest-aware chain pivot, so a tagged `+` chain keeps its marker and loses its glue / head-break rewrites

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-ADD-REBUILD-PLAIN
arms.note: a rewritten tagged `+` chain comes back under a plain `Group` with its rest-awareness dropped, so it spills one column past the limit again

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-GLUE-TERNARY
arms.note: a rest-aware ternary pivot is forward-glued whenever anything in it opens, not only when its condition closes an opened group, so a ternary call argument hugs an opening paren branch the fork breaks before

arms.name: M-COLLAPSE-GLUE-REST-CHAIN-SKIPPED
arms.find:
case WrapBoundary(GroupWithRestProbe(IfBreak(_, fl))) if (restAwareGlues(gluedSide(fl, width), decisions, width)):
gluedSide(fl, width);
arms.note: a rest-aware `&&` / `+` chain whose trailing paren opens is no longer forward-glued, so it breaks before `|| (` instead of hugging the paren

arms.name: M-TAIL-RESOLVE-IGNORED
arms.note: the closing-line read ignores the request to read a conditional that cannot stay flat on its break side

arms.name: M-OFFER-WANTED-DROPS
arms.note: a host that filters its offers gets none, so the chain never lays itself out for the region break

arms.name: M-OFFER-COPIES-WHOLE
arms.note: a rewrite copies every node it walks instead of sharing what it leaves unchanged, so each offered alternative copies its host whole and nested hosts grow the Doc exponentially in depth

arms.name: M-OFFER-REPLACES-BOTH-SIDES
arms.find: f == flat ? n : BreakCommit(brk, f, token);
arms.replace: f == flat ? n : BreakCommit(walk(brk), f, token);
arms.note: an offer also rewrites the other breaks' alternatives it passes, so every nested host re-walks and re-copies all of them and a deep paren chain writes in a high power of its depth

arms.name: M-OFFER-REPLACED-COPIES
arms.note: an offer copies every node it walks again, both sides of every other break included, so each nested host copies the alternatives below it whole and the build grows exponentially with the nesting depth

arms.name: M-TRAIL-REGION-UNDER-COMMENT
arms.note: a comment in front of a region ending the list hides the region, so the trailing-comma knob writes `#end,` again

arms.name: M-LEAD-BLOCK-COMMENT-END
arms.note: the scan resumes inside the closing `*/` of a leading block comment and reads its `/` as the item's first token

arms.name: M-PAREN-REST-THRESHOLD-INEXACT
arms.note: a glued paren holding a chain with a lineLength threshold measures the rest of its line flat to the end instead of up to a later argument list that breaks, so it opens on a line that fits

arms.name: M-CHAIN-GLUE-THRESHOLD-FIRES
arms.find:
case WrapBoundary(GroupWithRestProbe(IfBreak(_, fl))) if (restAwareGlues(gluedSide(fl, width), decisions, width)):
gluedSide(fl, width);
arms.replace:
case WrapBoundary(GroupWithRestProbe(IfBreak(_, fl))) if (restAwareGlues(fl, decisions, width)):
fl;
arms.note: a rest-aware chain whose flat side a lineLength threshold partitions is not recognised as a glued infix chain, so it is never committed glued around its opened paren and breaks at its own operator instead

arms.name: M-CHAIN-COLLAPSE-THRESHOLD-FIRES
arms.note: an inner add-chain collapsed inside a broken outer one keeps its lineLength threshold, which fires past the limit and breaks the collapsed chain

arms.name: M-CHAIN-COLLAPSE-PROBED-THRESHOLD-FIRES
arms.note: an inner add-chain ending in a bare paren, collapsed inside a broken outer one, keeps its lineLength threshold, which fires past the limit and breaks it

arms.name: M-CHAIN-GLUE-PAREN-THRESHOLD-FIRES
arms.note: a chain in a paren of its own, committed glued around an opened paren, keeps its lineLength threshold, which measures the chain flat and breaks it after the commit

arms.name: M-CHAIN-GLUED-SIDE-DROPS-REACHED-THRESHOLD
arms.find: case IfWidthExceeds(n, _, notFired) if (n > width): gluedSide(notFired, width);
arms.note: a collapse drops every lineLength threshold on the chain's flat side, so a rule below the limit that the collapsed inner chain reaches never fires and the chain stays one over-threshold line

arms.name: M-GLUE-COMMENT-AFTER-DELIM
arms.note: a line comment after an open delimiter ends the natural first line on the comment, so a chain stops hugging `xs.foreach(t -> { // why`

arms.name: M-LINE-SPAN-IGNORES-TEXT-LINES
arms.note: a line break inside a token stops counting as leaving the line, so a body stands on a label that took two lines

arms.name: M-LINE-SPAN-BREAKS-FORCED-FLAT
arms.note: a forced-flat frame takes the breaking side, so a line break appears where the frame promised none

arms.name: M-LINE-SPAN-READS-WITHOUT-BEGIN
arms.note: a read with no begin in the render compares against the unset record and always takes the left side

arms.name: M-SETTLE-KEEPS-COMMITTED
arms.note: a committed break settled without a measure render is left in the Doc, which the collapse pass and the emit render never resolve

arms.name: M-SETTLE-SKIPS-TOKEN
arms.note: a break carrying a token is taken for settled, so resolve skips the measure render and leaves that break unresolved

arms.name: M-DECISIONS-OF-ANOTHER-DOC
arms.replace: return { doc: commit(doc, tokens, new DocIdentityMap()), decisions: taken };
arms.note: the measure decisions handed to CollapsePass are keyed by nodes of a Doc the pass does not rewrite
